Employers of Voat, What's Your Biggest "Dealbreaker"?

Blatant or willful? I'd rather deal with someone who is actually just not quite there than someone who is wasting their mind because they think it's cool to be stupid. At least I know where I stand with the former.
We work with radioactive materials. I do not have room for either.
All I am saying is if you are falling asleep in the interview, I won't hire you, but my boss will give you an offer on the spot.

Blatant lying. I hate when I can see a task undone and someone is telling me at that moment that they did in fact complete it. Or dropping/breaking/spilling something and denying it. Things are so much easier to fix in the moment rather than finding and dealing with it later. If I can't trust that you'll do the job right, you're useless to me.

People who don't even try to look good for an interview.

I ran a work experience program where I placed people in jobs for nonprofits. I get that the people I was helping were often in rough places in their lives but I was still suprised how many just didn't care to try at all. For every homeless person who did their best to look as clean and neat as they could I interviewed 20 lazy fucks we go just dumped a gallon of perfume on instead of bathing. (And I gave those homeless the jobs after hooking them up with places to get new clothes and take showers before work)
How did you know who did their best and who didn't?

If you come in filthy dirty, in so much perfume I could smell you when you entered the building, shirt unbuttoned with a greasy inappropriate t-shirt on underneath, dusted in fast food crumbs, and obviously didn't even comb your fingers through your hair? Pretty sure you didn't try at all. Wash your face in a public bathroom sink, button your shirt, take the cigarette out from behind your ear, and at least TRY to look presentable. Sit up straight and don't start telling me about how you smell like booze because you were at this "fucking bitchin party" last night and you only just woke up at 2pm.

To contrast the homeless people I met who washed up as best they could and at least TRIED to look and act presentable? There's no contest as to who I would hire.
I'm not an employer but my boss told me about this guy he interviewed who said, when asked about his goals, that he wanted to go barefoot for a year straight. My boss was thoroughly unimpressed.
Why is that a bad goal to have? He probably didn't mean working in an office and living in a city while barefoot, more so a tropical beach or something.
But it was a job interview. They are asking about career goals. If going barefoot for a year is the best you can come up with, it reflects very poorly on you as a candidate.

People will say things like this to end an interview early. Your boss should examine what he said that made the candidate lose interest in working for your company. If you're constantly getting off the wall answers in interviews, you've got a bad interviewer.
For me it's very important to have problem solvers at all levels. On this age it's ridiculous to ask your boss how to use a function from excel when you can just Google it.

Late to the interview, especially with no advance warning - if I get a call 10 minutes before you're supposed to be here with "Hey, I'm in traffic", I might think less of your ability to plan ahead, but it's not an instant no. If you're late, though, and didn't call, I take three things from that - a) you're unreliable; b) you're too selfish or inconsiderate to respect other people's time (if you don't value mine, you surely won't value your coworkers', either); and c) you don't really want this job.

That gross incompetence, unreliability, and lying are deal breakers goes without saying. Beyond those it really depends on individual performance and on the dynamic he/she has with coworkers. Some people are flat out toxic and disruptive to the group but would be fine, perhaps even outstanding, by themselves. You always try to maximize a person's strengths but it's not always possible. For instance if you're hiring a receptionist then they had better be good on the phones and keeping track of details.

So for me usually the deal breaker was when it became obvious that the person I hired was unsuited for the position ether because everyone hated him/her or because they we not that good at it. You'd think it would be obvious in the interviews but you'd be wrong.

I work hand-in-hand with my manager. He's convinced the so-called online "personality tests" don't tell the entire story so we go through a lot of the low-scoring ones as that's really the entire pool we have to choose from. I've come up with instant skips and this is how we apply them.

Email Addresses: People, if you're using RealDownAssN***a2001@gmail.com don't realistically expect that we're going to call you. If that is your email address you can simply create one like MrNoDaysOff@gmal.com or something that that. Hell, these days people use their real names in their email addresses. If you can make a play on that that's clever without portraying yourself like a total douche, you'll probably get a call but StraightUpOGDawg@gmail.com shows us that you're probably coming to work with your pants halfway off your ass and none of us are taking chances on that.

Accomplishments: "I spent several hours trying to figure out what was wrong with that code I was working on until I found I'd transposed two characters. After that, my Black Box Project worked like a dream. Would you like to see it?" sounds more like an accomplishment to us. "I've only called in sick three times in three months,"...if we do hire you, consider it a miracle and if you're calling in sick that many times, don't expect that miracle to last.

Unwillingness to Learn: We look for that in the interview process and we look for it in the job. If you're not willing to learn, we're not willing to let you stay.

Past Theft Convictions: Two or more? Yeah it's not looking good pal.

References are all family members: Heh...good one...NEXT!

Longevity: If your "collection of careers" span only six months, guaranteed we'll take notes on why and then we'll check up on them. Don't hold your breath.
